label: thm:ftc2
title: Second Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
statement:
Let $f' : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be interval integrable on $[a,b]$, and let $F$ be continuous on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$ with right derivative $f'(x)$ at every $x \in (\min(a,b), \max(a,b))$, i.e.\ $\texttt{HasDerivWithinAt}\; F\; (f'\; x)\; (x, +\infty)\; x$. Then
\[
  \int_a^b f'(x)\,dx = F(b) - F(a).
\]
In Mathlib this is \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_eq\_sub\_of\_hasDeriv\_right}.
proof: This is a direct application of \texttt{intervalIntegral.integral\_eq\_sub\_of\_hasDeriv\_right}, given the continuity of $F$ on $[\min(a,b), \max(a,b)]$, the right-derivative hypothesis on the interior, and the integrability of $f'$.
